important.name: An issue named only in related_gh_issues counts as tracked, so it never gets an item
important.summary: catalog_issue_numbers (issues.py:44-49) adds `related_gh_issues` to the tracked set. The schema defines that list as open issues an item cross-references but does not resolve (TodoCatalog.schema.json:685). So an open issue that only shows up as related is hidden by `untracked`, and `add` refuses it (reshape.py:153, already in the catalog). Nothing in the catalog resolves it and no tool lets one be added. This depends on run order: in the catalog this PR commits, TODO-007 lists #80 as related (docs/TODO/RepoToDo.json:458-460). Had #81 been synced in an earlier batch than #80, #80 would have dropped off every later `untracked` run. Mentioned and tracked are not the same thing.
fix: Drop `related_gh_issues` from _item_numbers so only `gh_issues`, gh_issue sources, trackers, children, close candidates and research entries count as tracked. Add a test where an issue appears only as related and is still listed by find_untracked and accepted by add_items.

If counting related issues as tracked is intended, say so in the plan Design Decisions and in the issues.py module docstring, and have `untracked` print the related-only issues on a separate line so they are not silently lost.

important.name: add writes items the catalog schema rejects
important.summary:
_check_types (docstring: refuse a wrong-shaped value 'before it reaches scoring or the catalog') checks only base types. It does not enforce the TodoCatalog item rules: needs_decision true requires a non-empty decision_question and false requires null; status NEEDS_DECISION requires needs_decision true; code_snippet must start with a path:line header line; url must match ^https://\S+$; files must be unique; kind/impact/loe.size/blast_radius.level are enums and loe/blast_radius forbid extra keys. So a spec with {"status": "NEEDS_DECISION"} (needs_decision defaults False), with needs_decision true and no question (defaults to null), or with a free-text code_snippet passes, and _apply writes the catalog without validating it. The next `todo_sync.py check` then reports a schema error. A bad impact or LoE size is caught only by scoring, and that error names the temporary id ('cannot score add-new-1') rather than the spec item number.

Also (overall): _TYPE_RULES checks kind only as a non-empty string and needs_decision, decision_question, status independently. The schema (TodoCatalog.schema.json:628-638, 855-903) needs kind in its enum, a non-empty question when needs_decision is true (null otherwise) and needs_decision true for status NEEDS_DECISION. Such specs pass add and leave a T1 error, though todo-editor.md:144 says add refuses them.

Also (system_shape): todo-editor.md:144 and _check_types (reshape.py:130-134) say add refuses a wrong-shaped value. _TYPE_RULES (:110-127) checks kind, url and code_snippet only as strings: no kind enum, no ^https:// pattern, no path:line header. It also accepts extra keys in loe/blast_radius, non-string consumers, duplicate files, and needs_decision true with a null decision_question. _apply (:369-381) writes without schema validation, so T1 reports these only at finish, after the write.

Also (roast): _check_types (reshape.py:130-134) claims to refuse a wrong-shaped value before it reaches the catalog, and the agent (todo-editor.md:144) promises `add` refuses any other shape. It only checks that `kind` is a non-empty string, `code_snippet` is a string and `files`/`related_gh_issues` are lists. The item schema (TodoCatalog.schema.json:628-639, 705-716, 718-744) requires `kind` from a seven-value enum, `code_snippet` matching a path:line first-line pattern, unique `files` and `related_gh_issues`, and no extra keys in `blast_radius`. So `kind: chore`, a snippet with no path:line header, or the same path listed twice (the agent writes one path:line finding per review comment and lists the paths, so duplicates are likely) passes `add`, gets renumbered and written, and only `check` T1 catches it afterwards, on a catalog the agent then hand-edits. In short, the validator approves things the schema rejects.
fix: Before _apply writes, validate each built item (or the whole renumbered catalog) against TodoCatalog.schema.json `$defs/item` with the jsonschema validator that rules_todo.py already builds, and raise TodoSyncError('item N: ...') on the first error.

Extend _TYPE_RULES with the cross-field and enum rules: needs_decision vs decision_question, status NEEDS_DECISION implies needs_decision, code_snippet header pattern, url pattern, unique files, and enum checks for kind, impact, loe.size and blast_radius.level against the schema or ranking_method tables.
Add a kind enum rule and a coherence check after _check_types, with TYPE_CASES entries in tests/lib/test_todo_sync_add.py.
Or validate built items against the schema item definition before _renumber.
Validate each built item against TodoCatalog.schema.json $defs/item in add_items before _renumber, raising TodoSyncError with the item number and path.
Or narrow todo-editor.md:144 to the checked fields and say that T1 at finish catches the rest.

Before `_renumber` in add_items, validate each built item against the catalog schema `$defs/item` (the same schema T1 in rules_todo.py loads), with the temporary id/rank/priority swapped for valid placeholders, and raise TodoSyncError naming item n and the failing path.

Or extend _TYPE_RULES: `kind` in the schema enum, `code_snippet` against the schema pattern, `files`/`related_gh_issues` without duplicates (or dedupe them in _item_fields), `decision_question` a non-empty string when `needs_decision` is true, and refuse keys other than size/reasoning in `loe` and level/reasoning/consumers in `blast_radius`.

important.name: CLI add refusal never proves the catalog is left untouched
important.summary: test_add_refusal_exits_2 asserts only exit 2 and the bare substring 'problem:'. Any failure path passes it, including an unreadable spec or a crash turned into a problem line, and nothing checks that RepoToDo.json is byte-identical after the refusal. The lib refusal tests (test_refusals) exercise the pure add_items, never apply_add, so no test in the PR covers 'a refused add writes nothing', which is the safety property the agent's add call depends on.

Alternatively add a lib-level test calling apply_add with a refused spec and asserting the catalog bytes are unchanged.

minor.name: untracked: malformed gh output crashes with a traceback, and truncation at the list limit is silent
minor.summary:
open_issues calls json.loads(out) on the `gh issue list` stdout without a guard. main() catches only ConfigError, TodoSyncError and OSError, so a non-JSON reply (for example a gh warning on stdout) ends in a traceback instead of a 'problem:' line. A repository with more than LIST_LIMIT (1000) open issues is also cut off without notice, so untracked under-reports.

Also (roast): open_issues calls `json.loads(out)` (issues.py:96) with no guard. main() catches only ConfigError, TodoSyncError and OSError (todo_sync.py:211), so a non-JSON stdout from `gh issue list` (a proxy page, a gh warning on stdout) raises JSONDecodeError with a traceback. The plan review focus says gh failing exits 2 with one `problem:` line. reviews.py already catches ValueError for the same reason. The issue list never got that treatment.

Also (roast): `gh issue list --limit 1000` (issues.py:21, 94-95) silently stops at 1000 issues. A repository with more open issues gets an `untracked` result that looks complete and is not, and the skill reports it as the full list.
fix: Wrap json.loads in try/except ValueError and raise TodoSyncError('gh issue list returned no JSON: ...').
When len(rows) == LIST_LIMIT, raise or add a warning line saying the list may be truncated.
Wrap the parse in open_issues: catch ValueError and raise TodoSyncError with the message gh issue list returned no JSON, chained from the original, and check that the result is a list.
When `len(rows) == LIST_LIMIT`, raise TodoSyncError (or print a `warning:` line) saying the listing hit the limit and may be incomplete.

fix: Check snapshot_name(day) against todo.snapshots.name_pattern before write_atomic, so the refusal happens before any file is written.
Catch TodoSyncError from render_snapshot and re-raise it with the created catalog path and a 'run todo_sync.py render' hint.
Check the snapshot name against todo.snapshots.name_pattern before write_atomic.

minor.name: Tracked-number branches are redundant in the fixture, so dropping one passes
minor.summary: issues.py documents an item as tracked through gh_issues, related_gh_issues or a gh_issue source. The fixture records issue 11 both in gh_issues and as a '#11' source, and no item has related_gh_issues, so test_tracked_numbers_cover_every_record still passes with either the gh_issues or the sources branch deleted, and with the related_gh_issues branch deleted. add_items reuses catalog_issue_numbers for its duplicate refusal, so a regression there would also let an add duplicate an item.
fix: Add a parametrized test that builds a catalog item carrying only one of gh_issues, related_gh_issues or a gh_issue source (each naming a distinct number) and asserts that number is in tracked_numbers.

minor.name: find_untracked's 'sorted by number' contract is never exercised
minor.summary: Every test feeds open issues already in ascending order (or with a single untracked issue), so removing the sorted() call in find_untracked would not fail any test, although the docstring promises sorted rows and the CLI prints them in that order.
fix: In test_find_untracked_lists_only_unrecorded_issues, feed two untracked issues in descending order (for example 300 then 200) and assert the rows come back as [200, 300].

minor.name: Budget rule 'first review is always kept whole' is untested
minor.summary: fetch_reviews documents that the first review is kept whole even when it alone exceeds the budget. test_budget_truncates_and_flags uses a first review (30 chars) under the budget (40), so changing the guard from 'if kept and ...' to 'if ...' passes every test while silently dropping an oversized only review.
fix: Add a case with budget=10 and one 30-character review; assert it is returned whole and truncated is False, then add a second review and assert truncated is True.

minor.summary: The module docstring says it covers 'The untracked and add subcommands', but test_init_creates_the_catalog_and_refuses_a_second_run also drives the init subcommand.
fix: Reword the first docstring line to 'The init, untracked and add subcommands of scripts/todo_sync.py, ...'.
